Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Tools, fasteners & household repair

broken adjective

also it’s broken, cracked, smashed, broken down

classical

Cato Agr. 144: nisi quae vetustāte frāctae erunt
Caes. BG 4.29.3: complūribus nāvibus frāctīs (Lewis & Short)

1frāctus: long a (Lewis & Short leaves it unmarked). De Vaan 239, s.v. frangō: “The long vowel of fractus is due to Lachmann’s Law.” Traupman 106 marks it too. Ruling: Lachmann’s law: āctus, lēctus, frāctus.

frāctus1, frācta, frāctum

adjective (participle of frangō, frangere, frēgī, frāctum)

“It’s broken” is frāctum est; “who broke it?”, quis frēgit? Broken into little pieces is comminūtus (see break into pieces); a string or a balloon that has burst is ruptus (see burst); a broken bone, see fracture.

Other words

  • vitium facere — develop a fault, be damaged

    phrase; in the perfect, vitium fēcit · also used · classical · Cic. Top. 15: sī aedēs corruērunt vitiumve fēcērunt (Lewis & Short)

    Cicero’s phrase for a house that has been damaged. For a machine that has stopped working it is our suggestion.

Examples

  • scālae ita utī datae erunt, ita redditō, nisi quae vetustāte frāctae erunt

    return the ladders as they were given, except any that have broken with ageCato Agr. 144

  • frangere dum metuis, frangēs crystallina: peccant sēcūrae nimium sollicitaeque manūs

    while you are afraid of breaking the glass, you will break it: hands that are too careless slip, and so do hands that are too carefulMart. 14.111.1–2

See also break into pieces, burst, fracture, repair, mend, whole.
